content:
STEP 1：作業場所を作る
まず、素材・投稿・開発・ログを分けて管理する。
例：
/video_raw
/video_export
/x_posts
/system
/logs
/tasks
このようにフォルダを分けて、
Hermes Agentがどこを見ればいいか、
Codexがどこに動画を書き出せばいいか、
Claude Codeがどこを開発すればいいかを決める。
ここを曖昧にすると、
AIが毎回違う場所を見に行って作業が崩れる。
STEP 2：タスク管理の型を作る

次に、Hermes Agentが扱うタスクの型を決める。
例えば、
・タスク名
・目的
・担当AI
・入力素材
・出力形式
・期限
・承認が必要か
・完了条件
・ログ保存先

これをテンプレ化する。
AIに自由に任せるのではなく、
毎回この型に沿って動かす。
これで、
「何を頼んだか」
「誰が担当したか」
「どこまで終わったか」
が見えるようになる。

STEP 3：Hermes Agentに司令塔ルールを渡す
Hermes Agentには、
最初にこういうルールを持たせる。
・人間の依頼を必ずタスクに分解する
・動画編集はCodexに振る
・開発はClaude Codeに振る
・X投稿は自分で下書きを作る
・公開前には必ず確認を挟む
・失敗した処理はログに残す
・反応データを見て次の改善タスクを作る
このルールを入れておくことで、
Hermes Agentは単なるチャットAIではなく、
業務全体を管理するPMのように動く。
STEP 4：Codexに動画編集パイプラインを作らせる
Codexには、
動画素材を受け取って、
編集済み動画を出力する流れを作らせる。
流れはこう。
素材動画を読み込む
↓
音声を文字起こしする
↓
重要そうな部分を抽出する
↓
ショート動画用にカットする
↓
テロップを生成する
↓
9:16や1:1に変換する
↓
BGMや効果音を必要に応じて追加
↓
完成動画を書き出す
この時点では、
完璧な編集を目指さない。

最初は、
「動画をアップしたら自動でショート動画候補が3本出る」
くらいで十分。
人間はその中から選んで、
必要な部分だけ直す。
これだけでも、
編集者に毎回依頼する作業のかなりの部分を短縮できる。

STEP 5：Claude Codeに管理システムを作らせる

Claude Codeには、
AIたちが作った成果物を管理するシステムを作らせる。

例えば、
・動画素材一覧
・編集済み動画一覧
・X投稿の下書き一覧
・投稿ステータス管理
・承認ボタン
・投稿後の反応記録
・改善メモ
・次回タスクの自動生成
こういう管理画面があると、
AIが作ったものが散らばらない。
ここで重要なのは、
AIが作業する場所と、人間が確認する場所を分けること。

AIは裏側で大量に作る。
人間は管理画面で確認する。
OKなら公開。
NGなら修正指示。
この形にすると、
人間は作業者ではなく、
最終判断者になる。
STEP 6：Hermes AgentにX運用を任せる

X運用では、
Hermes Agentが以下を担当する。

・動画から投稿ネタを作る
・1投稿用の短文を作る
・スレッド構成を作る
・画像付き投稿の文章を作る
・引用ポスト案を作る
・リプライ案を作る
・投稿後の反応を分析する
・反応が良かった型を保存する
・次の投稿ネタを提案する
例えば、
動画が1本ある場合、
Hermes Agentはそこから、
・短文ポスト
・長文ポスト
・スレッド
・図解用テキスト
・ショート動画の告知文
・リプライ誘導文
をまとめて作る。
それをCodexが作った動画と組み合わせて、
投稿候補として管理画面に並べる。
STEP 7：公開前に人間が確認する
ここはかなり大事。
完全自動で投稿まで行くと、
誤投稿、表現ミス、規約違反、誤情報、炎上リスクが出る。

だから最初は必ず、
AIが作る
↓
管理画面に並べる
↓
人間が確認
↓
OKなら投稿
↓
投稿後の反応をAIが分析

という流れにする。
最初から完全自動化を狙うのではなく、
半自動化から始めるのが現実的。
STEP 8：反応データを次の改善に回す

投稿したら終わりではない。
Hermes Agentが、
インプレッション、いいね、保存、プロフィールクリック、返信、フォロー増加などを見て、
次の改善タスクを作る。
例えば、

「この投稿はフックが強かった」
「動画付きの方が伸びた」
「技術説明より導入手順の方が反応が良い」
「短文より長文の方が保存された」
「図解付きの方がクリック率が高い」

こういう分析をもとに、
次の投稿パターンを作る。

ここまでつながると、
AIが単発で作業するのではなく、
投稿 → 反応 → 改善 → 再投稿
のループができる。

この仕組みの本質は、
AIに仕事を丸投げすることではない。

人間がやっていた、
・動画編集
・投稿作成
・システム改善
・分析
・改善案作成
・管理業務
をAIごとに分担させること。
Codexは動画編集の自動化。
Claude Codeはシステム開発。
Hermes AgentはX運用と全体管理。
この3つをつなぐと、
1人でも、
編集者・エンジニア・SNS運用担当がいるチームのように動ける。
最初に作るべきMVPはこれ。

動画素材をアップする
Codexがショート動画候補を作る
Hermes AgentがX投稿文を作る
Claude Codeが投稿管理画面を作る

人間が確認して投稿する
Hermes Agentが反応を分析する

次の改善タスクを自動で作る

ここまでできれば、
X運用・動画編集・システム開発が
1つの流れでつながる。

つまり、
これからのAI活用で大事なのは、
「どのAIが一番賢いか」ではなく、
どのAIに、どの仕事を任せるか。

Hermes Agentを司令塔にして、
Codexを動画編集担当、
Claude Codeを開発担当にする。
これだけで、
AIはただのチャット相手ではなく、
実際に業務を進めるチームになる。

・今回初めて人とAIに本物の「認知ループ」が生まれる

■問われているのは
・ツール導入の話ではない
・AIが人と組織の専門性を吸収しコモディティ化する世界で、いかに学び・IP・差別化を続けられるか

■全企業が持つべき2つの資本
・人的資本：知識・判断・人間関係・創意・パターン認識
・トークン資本：自社が構築し所有するAI能力

Claude Code、めちゃくちゃ便利だけど高いですよね。
私も200ドルプランで自動チャージをオンにしていたら、3日で約450ドル（10万円弱）の追加課金が発生しました‥

UberやMicrosoftでも「予算オーバーだから使用を控えよう」という話が出るほど。AIエージェント時代は、性能を保ちつつコストと向き合う運用がカギになります。

この動画では、無駄なトークンを節約する「秘伝のタレ」を初心者向けにまとめました。

特に、
・/clear と /compact の使い分け
・CLAUDE.mdの圧縮とスキルへの切り出し
・Opusを使いすぎず Sonnet 4.6 を基本に
・スコープ指定とプランモードで無駄スキャンを防ぐ

このあたりを押さえるだけで、かなり変わります。
そして最強の防衛策は「自動チャージをオフ」にすること。ここはマストです。

Claude Codeを使う人は、この動画でコスト最適化をマスターしてください。

content:
I've built dozens of businesses.

If I lost it all tomorrow and had to rebuild it from scratch without much cash or talent, here's exactly what I'd do:

1. Start selling before you build

Your biggest advantage starting out is speed.

If you can move from idea to launch in 24 hours while your competitor is scheduling a planning meeting for next quarter, you win.

One of our academy members literally posted a Facebook rant about his local trash company and dropped a pre-sell link in the comments. He hit $13k MRR before owning a single truck or license.

2. Pick an industry where the odds are stacked in your favor

Those aren't the ones everybody's bragging about.

• Information businesses have a 29% survival rate after 10 years. 
• Manufacturing and agriculture? 49%.

There's actually an inverse relationship between the age of the owner and your odds of making money. 

The older the owner, the more likely that business stays solvent when you buy it.

Which brings me to...

3. Look for the shortest path to ownership inside it

Right now, that path is the Boomer exit.

41% of all small businesses are owned by people aged 62 or older. Most of them are near or at retirement and have no one to sell to. 

Which means thousands of businesses are about to go up for grabs in the next 10 years. 

Get your hands on one of them and scale the s**t out of it. 

4. Buy businesses that pay you whether the economy is up or down

The ones I'd target look something like this: 

• Same owner since 1987
• Stable revenue for the last 5+ years
• 10-15 employees
• No marketing
• Old website

Adding tech to a business run by a 70 year old is easier than running the 1,000th social media app on the market.

5. Sell to the rich

The best customers to sell to are the ones with money. 

If I'm starting a lawn care business, I'm not building a $99 mowing package for the masses. I'm selling a $10k commercial package for high-end clients who want a better service.

What I’d focus on to sell to affluent buyers:

• Scarcity: Limited availability, limited access
• Privacy: Things others can't get into or know about
• Exclusivity: The club with a real barrier to entry
• Convenience: Their time has a dollar value and they'd rather pay than wait
• Status: Put their name on it and they'll write a bigger check

Anchor every offer to one of these 5. And don’t discount!

6. Build an audience while running the biz

The last thing you want is being dependent on paid ads to reach your customers.

Customer acquisition costs are up 3-5x since 2014 (and only going up from here). Paying for ads is renting someone else's audience by the month.

How I'd build my own:

• Newsletter → owned audience, no algorithm that decides who sees your posts
• YouTube → highest ROI of any social platform right now
• Social media accounts → post organic content for free and use the best performing ones as ads

Much easier to run a business when you don't need to pay to reach your customers. 

7. Wire AI into the back-end from day one

I'd automate every repetitive touchpoint that doesn't need a human...

• SEO
• Scheduling
• Customer intake
• Lead qualification
• Follow-up sequences

So the business runs without me in the routine work.

And the humans stay where the magic actually needs to happen: sales, customer service, and hiring.

-

tl;dr

> Pick the unsexy business in the right industry
> Run it lean
> Sell to customers who can pay
> With distribution you own
> And AI doing the repetitive work

If you do these things, 2026 will be your richest year yet.

title: Steal Pixar's Secret Storytelling Framework (To Write More Compelling Stories In The Next 5 Minutes)
content:
The single most powerful skill to advance your career:
Storytelling.
If you can tell compelling stories, you can:
- Get a raise
- Earn a promotion
- Even shape the world
And no one tells better stories than Pixar.

They've made over $14 billion at the box office.

And their most recent film (Hoppers) is the 2nd highest-grossing original film this decade.
This movie exploded right out of the gate with this little guy becoming an instant meme everywhere.
Luckily, you don't need to be a billion-dollar company to master storytelling.
Just use these 22 Pixar storytelling rules:
Back in 2011, Pixar storyboard artist Emma Coats shared their "22 Rules For Storytelling.”
Let’s dive in:

Rule #1: You admire a character for trying more than for their successes.

Your audience loves the story - the path - the ups and downs.
For stories, brands, and products - focus on the how and why (and less on the what).

Rule #2: You gotta keep in mind what's interesting to you as an audience, not what's fun to do as a writer.

They can be very different.
This is similar to Craig Clemens's first rule of writing:
You, the writer, are completely irrelevant.
Focus on delivering to the audience.

Rule #3: Trying for theme is important, but you won't see what the story is actually about til you're at the end of it. Now rewrite.

Your original idea rarely ends up the same as your final idea.
So don't overthink it - take something, get it going, then refine it.

Rule #4: Use a proven "story spine"

"Once upon a time there was ___." "Every day, ___." "One day ___." "Because of that, ___." "Because of that, ___. Until finally ___."
This one is my favorite.
Whether you're a writer, an entrepreneur, or a brand, you can use this "story spine" to effortlessly create a narrative.

Rule #5: Simplify. Focus. Combine characters. Hop over detours. You'll feel like you're losing valuable stuff but it sets you free.

This goes far beyond storytelling.
The goal for every writer, marketer, or entrepreneur should be to add constraints and do more with less.

Rule #6: What is your character good at, comfortable with? Throw the polar opposite at them. Challenge them. How do they deal?

Think of this like the inversion technique.
What is everyone in your niche saying?
How can you say the same things, but in different ways?

Rule #7: Come up with your ending before you figure out your middle. Seriously. Endings are hard, get yours working up front.

Stories, sales pages, brand pitches - always start with the end in mind and work backward from there.

Rule #8: Finish your story, let go even if it's not perfect. In an ideal world you have both, but move on. Do better next time.

Reminds me of this famous quote:
"No book is ever finished, it is merely abandoned."
Don't let perfectionism keep you from publishing.

Rule #9: When you're stuck, make a list of what WOULDN'T happen next. Lots of times the material to get you unstuck will show up.

This is the ultimate hack to overcome writer's block.
Make a list of everything you don't want to write about to get the juices flowing.

Rule #10: Pull apart the stories you like. What you like in them is a part of you; you've got to recognize it before you can use it.

90% of being a good writer or storyteller is being a good noticer.
Notice when things resonate with you and start asking why.

Rule #11: Putting it on paper lets you start fixing it. If it stays in your head, a perfect idea, you'll never share it with anyone.

Your head is the worst place to store ideas.
This is why Tim Ferriss commits to writing 2 crappy pages per day.
Focus on getting the raw material.

Rule #12: Discount the 1st thing that comes to mind. And the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th – get the obvious out of the way. Surprise yourself.

This reminds me of Julian Shapiro's Creativity Faucet idea.
To find your best ideas, you need to unclog all the junk first.

Rule #13: Give your characters opinions. Passive/malleable might seem likable to you as you write, but it's poison to the audience.

Your opinions should make your audience take a stand.
No "it seems" or "maybes" or "potentiallys" take a stand and don't hedge.

Rule #14: Why must you tell THIS story? What's the belief burning within you that your story feeds off of? That's the heart of it.

Nothing to add on this one.
It's one of the best reflection questions I've ever come across.

Rule #15: If you were your character, in this situation, how would you feel? Honesty lends credibility to unbelievable situations.

The best writers and storytellers strike the balance of authenticity (like telling personal stories) while still providing value to the audience.

Rule #16: What are the stakes? Give us a reason to root for the character. What happens if they don't succeed? Stack the odds against.

"Stakes" are part of the foundation on which every good story is built.
For more, check out Matthew Dick's book Storyworthy.

Rule #17: No work is ever wasted. If it's not working, let go and move on it'll come back around to be useful later.

You won't always put our your best stuff.
And trying to do so is impossible (and leads to burnout).
So focus on showing up - consistency creates competence.

Rule #18: You have to know yourself: the difference between doing your best & fussing. Story is testing, not refining.

Too often people get caught up in trying to plan every step from A to Z.
And this "planning" is really procrastination in disguise.

Rule #19: Coincidences to get characters into trouble are great.

But coincidences to get them out of it are cheating.

Rule #20: Exercise: take the building blocks of a movie you dislike. How would you rearrange them into what you DO like?

You can use this for every creative medium.
When something doesn't resonate with you (an article, a tweet, an ad, a story) ask why.
Then, make it better.

Rule #21: You gotta identify with your situation/characters, can't just write 'cool'. What would make YOU act that way?

This goes both ways - you need to put yourself in your character's shoes AND your audience's shoes.
Make your listener feel understood (through authenticity).

Rule #22: What's the essence of your story? Most economical telling of it? If you know that, you can build from there.

And the best for last - ask yourself: what are you really trying to say (in as few words as possible).
Strip away everything that distracts from that goal.

Rule #16: What are the stakes? Give us a reason to root for the character. What happens if they don't succeed? Stack the odds against.

"Stakes" are part of the foundation on which every good story is built.
For more, check out Matthew Dick's book Storyworthy.

Rule #17: No work is ever wasted. If it's not working, let go and move on it'll come back around to be useful later.

You won't always put our your best stuff.
And trying to do so is impossible (and leads to burnout).
So focus on showing up - consistency creates competence.

Rule #18: You have to know yourself: the difference between doing your best & fussing. Story is testing, not refining.

Too often people get caught up in trying to plan every step from A to Z.
And this "planning" is really procrastination in disguise.

Rule #19: Coincidences to get characters into trouble are great.

But coincidences to get them out of it are cheating.

Rule #20: Exercise: take the building blocks of a movie you dislike. How would you rearrange them into what you DO like?

You can use this for every creative medium.
When something doesn't resonate with you (an article, a tweet, an ad, a story) ask why.
Then, make it better.

Rule #21: You gotta identify with your situation/characters, can't just write 'cool'. What would make YOU act that way?

This goes both ways - you need to put yourself in your character's shoes AND your audience's shoes.
Make your listener feel understood (through authenticity).

Rule #22: What's the essence of your story? Most economical telling of it? If you know that, you can build from there.

And the best for last - ask yourself: what are you really trying to say (in as few words as possible).
Strip away everything that distracts from that goal.

title: 4 years. 17,500 founders. 1 lesson.
content:
You wake up.
You open your phone and Slack is on fire.
2 people on your team urgently need you (again).
You’re posting contentbut no one is biting.
Your calendar is packed with meetings – but you hardly want to be on any of them.
Your revenue is growing. But profit is stagnant. Your profit margin is steadily declining.
And worst off?
Your freedom is crumbling.
And it’s the whole reason you became an entrepreneur in the first place… but your time is dwindling though.
You have less time for the things you love, nature, adventure, and random side quests and these days even when you take them, you don’t feel psychologically free, your mind is always racing because the business isn’t where it needs to be.
You want founder freedom. You’re experiencing founder chaos.
You keep telling yourself, “I need help.” You know you can’t keep going on like this.
What you actually need is less complexity.
You want a lean team the leads and makes decision without needing constant babysitting.
You want to be a CEO – not a Chief Everything Officer.
You want a founder-led brand the converts clients from content automatically, not be stuck on a content hamster wheel wondering what you’re going to post the next day.
You want more profit, more peace, and more freedom.
Freedom (to me) is 20 hours a week to think, scheme, and plot (preferably a cozy home and environment with lots of nature).
It’s being able to go for a walk and have peace of mind (not constantly fearing what fire is going to need your attention next). You can’t keep going on like this. Something has got to give.
It’s time to become the architect of your company – instead of the operator trapped inside of it.
You want a company that gets simpler as it grows. And you deserve it.
That’s the whole reason 4 years ago, I started Founder OS.
Since then, I’ve helped more than 17,500 founders scale their founder-led brands, convert clients from content, streamline their operations, and build simple, peaceful, profitable companies that give them more freedom: time freedom, financial freedom, and mental freedom.
I’ve watched founders like Michelle Garabito go from unproven offers to $5M/year.
I’ve helped founders like Liam Ottley go from confused offer to 8-figures and 750,000 subscribers on YouTube.
I helped legends like Steve Gatena (Pray dot com) scale his LinkedIn to 100K followers, start a successful podcast, and drive new clients from organic content.
But on the other hand, I’ve watched some founders go from happy to miserable in their journey (I’ve been on over 70 free workshops with 28,000 people the last 4 years, so I’ve seen it all!) The strange part? Their lack of revenue isn’t the variable that makes most founders miserable. It’s the lack of simplicity.
Here’s the hard truth: Complexity is the ultimate killer of freedom.
The founders I see suffer and having the hardest time have:
-  Too many offers
-  Too many employees
-  Too many meetings
-  Too many tools
-  Too many projects going on (they suffer from idea indigestion, they are constantly getting lost in shiny object syndrome)
Here’s the deal…
Most businesses don’t die from a lack of opportunity. They die from too many opportunities and not knowing what to prioritize.
And they leave a ton of cash on the table because they distract themselves by making things way to complex.
Making money is simple. Freedom is simple. Having fun is simple. Building a business you love is simple. The key is to delete all the noise. Delete the dumb distractions. The BS that clogs up your machine and causes you to be running something you hardly even recognize.
That’s why I built Founder OS Velocity.
The premise behind everything I’ve built has been one core thing:
How do you build a business that increases your aliveness as it scales?
It’s not just me helping people with their operating systems. It’s not just me helping you build a founder-led brand and social media machine.
At a core level, it’s really about:
How do you build a business that gets simpler as it grows?

Founder OS turns 4 this month!!
The community and experience that I’ve built and refined from leaning into my calling in life is growing up so fast :) (I’m having a proud dad moment.)
I wanted to do something special to celebrate this and celebrate YOU. The founder that has been a part of this journey. And a part of the founder freedom movement.

-  A private 1:1 call with me
-  Access to 1:1s with my C-Suite
-  And cutting edge AI systems and skills to help you execute your organic content (that maintains your voice and soul and eliminates any slop)
That’s over $30,000 in value. I loooove helping founders. And as Founder OS turns 4, I am more determined and fired up than ever to go above and beyond to help you transform your life and business.
You can book a call with my COO Don to join Founder OS today (or join now at $5k/month for 6 months).
If you’re reading this and resonate with what I’m saying then this is your sign. This is the best time ever to join Founder OS, the price will be increasing July 1 and the bonuses will be gone.
We are investing more than ever in AI systems. We are giving founders access 1:1 with my legendary team, my CMO Nick, my COO Don, my Chief of Staff Claire – the same team that helped me scale my brand to 3M+ people, remove me from operations (saving me 30 hours a week), and the team behind everything you see from me online. These are my Personal Board of Advisors, and now you have access to them too.
And you get my entire Founder Operating System:
-  Content GPS: Your custom content strategy across your core platforms. What to post, where, how often, and why.
-  Content templates: The exact frameworks I use to convert my organic audience into clients.
-  Lead magnet and tool frameworks: So you're building an owned audience from day one (and control your destiny).
-  Founder AI Systems:  Your AI team. Not one chatbot, a team of specialist agents.
- My personal AI team I use to run a $15M brand, trained on 18 years experience,and data from serving over 17,500 founder-led brands. It produces content assets in your voice, based on your brand positioning and content strategy. LinkedIn posts, Instagram carousel copy, lead magnets, and YouTube outlines are all crafted by custom skills based on my experience producing 48,000 pieces of content and growing organic audiences to 16,800,000 followers.
This next year is going to be the most magical yet. And it’s all about doubling down on our mission to make your founder journey joyful.
Join Founder OS Velocity today by booking a call here with my COO Don.
Now is the time to move. Like, literally, right now.

I can’t wait to see you on the inside.
Let’s go!
